title: Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2017
short_title: Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2017

speeches.speaker: Richard Marles
speeches.brief: The bill creates the Defence Force Rehabilitation and Compensation Act (DRCA) as an exact replica of the SRCA for Defence members, transferring all veterans’ legislation under the Minister for Veterans’ Affairs. Labor supported the bill after securing assurances that no veteran would be worse off, but raised concerns about inadequate consultation and potential future alignment of legislation.

speeches.speaker: Meryl Swanson
speeches.brief: The Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016 was supported as a positive step toward a military-specific compensation scheme, but concerns were raised over the proposed Henry VIII clause and the need for a first principles review of the Department of Veterans' Affairs. The government's allocation of 85 per cent of DVA funding for the next financial year was criticised as insufficient for holistic reform.

speeches.speaker: Tim Hammond
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, arguing that separating Defence Force compensation from the main Act is a pragmatic move to simplify the system for injured veterans and workers.

speeches.speaker: Luke Gosling
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, acknowledging it was not perfect and could have had more consultation, but argued it would reduce red tape and provide a commonsense approach for veterans; they urged the Minister for Veterans' Affairs to re-dedicate to caring for servicemen and women.

speeches.speaker: Luke Gosling
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, which consolidates all veterans’ compensation, rehabilitation and benefits under the Minister for Veterans’ Affairs by replacing the SRCA with a new DRCA covering only Defence members and their families. The speaker also raised concerns about DVA’s adversarial relationship with veterans and slow claim processes, noted a need for a level 3 advocate in Darwin, and acknowledged local veteran organisations including the Vietnam Veterans Association of Australia NT branch, which plans to rename to Veterans Australia NT.

speeches.speaker: Ross Hart
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016 is a positive development that creates a military-specific compensation scheme (the DRCA) under the Minister for Veterans' Affairs, and stated that Labor supports the bill. The speaker also noted that 291 veterans died by suicide between 2001 and 2014, compared to 41 on active duty, and cautiously approved the minister's announcement on mental health conditions.

speeches.speaker: Madeleine King
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, which creates a new military-specific compensation scheme (DRCA) for Defence Force members and their families, transferring responsibility for all veterans legislation to the Minister for Veterans' Affairs. The speaker also raised concerns about the Department of Veterans' Affairs' consultation practices with ex-service organisations and highlighted the need for better support for veterans transitioning to civilian life, noting higher suicide rates among veterans, particularly young men aged 18-24.

speeches.speaker: Warren Snowdon
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, arguing it would rationalise veterans' compensation by quarantining Defence Force members from future SRCA amendments and placing all veterans acts under the Minister for Veterans' Affairs, while emphasising the unique nature of military service.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016, arguing it would improve support for defence personnel and veterans, citing past failures and statistics including 325 certified suicide deaths of ADF members between 2001 and 2015 and 45,000 veterans with mental health disabilities.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: The Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Defence Force) Bill 2016 creates the DRC Act, a military-specific compensation scheme for Defence members who served between 1 December 1998 and 1 July 2004, mirroring existing SRCA provisions without conferring new rights.
